prose: An essay argues the games industry is having its 'reap what you sow' moment: AI decompilation advances led by Claude Opus 5.5 are pumping out browser ports and native PC recompilations of games daily, and publishers can't keep up. Epic Games is DMCA-ing posts featuring a browser-playable Fortnite recreation while Microsoft stood up 'Xbox Labs' with a note invoking 75 years of game history.

Tim Sweeney responded to the karma charge by separating the pieces: Epic does not let people use Fortnite IP without permission or compensation, while it does restrict AI training on Unreal Engine and MetaHuman outputs. The author's point: publishers that admitted to using AI tools are now discovering those same tools turned against their own IP.
highlights: AI decompilation floods the web with browser ports and recompilations of games
Epic DMCAs a browser-playable Fortnite recreation; Microsoft launches 'Xbox Labs'
Sweeney: IP use without permission is still barred; AI training on UE/MetaHuman outputs restricted
Framed as the industry's 'you reap what you sow' moment
